summary: Page navigation for a table or list. Renders prev/next arrows, a truncated run of page numbers, and an optional rows-per-page Select.
useWhen: a result set is split into pages and the user needs to move between them
the total number of pages is known — the numbered run needs a last page to anchor to

useInstead.when: the total is unknown or unbounded, as with a cursor-based or infinite feed
useInstead.why: a numbered pager has to draw a last page; with no total there is nothing to draw, and a bare Load more button is honest about that

useInstead.when: the user is moving between peer views rather than through one long list
useInstead.why: pagination implies a sequence with a position; tabs are peers in any order

useInstead.when: it is navigation between pages of the app rather than pages of data

numbered.use: the default — prev, the page numbers, next. Use wherever the numbers fit

simple.use: prev, "Page N of M", next. For drawers, narrow columns and mobile, where a numbered run would wrap or truncate to uselessness

lg.use: roomy layouts, and touch targets on tablet

guarantees: the whole control is a landmark — a `nav` with an accessible name, defaulting to "Pagination"
the current page carries `aria-current="page"`, not `aria-pressed`: this is a position in a set, not a toggle
every cell has an explicit label — "Go to page 4", "Go to previous page" — so a screen reader never announces a bare digit
the ellipsis is `aria-hidden` and not focusable: it marks absent pages, and a tab stop that does nothing when activated is worse than no tab stop
in `simple`, the "Page N of M" text is an `aria-live="polite"` region, because the page can change without anything else on screen announcing it
prev and next are genuinely `disabled` at the ends rather than styled to look it
the focus ring shows for keyboard focus only, and hover does not latch on touch
requires: `aria-label` when more than one Pagination is on a page — two identically named landmarks are two indistinguishable landmarks
`pageSize` when `showPageSize` is set, or the rows-per-page Select renders with nothing selected

antiPatterns.avoid: passing `pageCount={0}` for an empty result set
antiPatterns.instead: render EmptyState and no pager — the component clamps to a single page, which draws a lone disabled `1` that says a page exists when none does
switch to `type="simple"`. Widening the run past the container is the problem truncation exists to solve, and it reappears one breakpoint down
it is 1-based, matching what the numbers say. An off-by-one here is silent — the pager looks right and fetches the wrong rows
